title: Cinematography and Video Synthesis
answer: Text to video, virtual lensing, digital doubles, storyboarding and frame interpolation.

children.name: Text to Video, Physics and Continuity
children.blurb: Text to video covers systems that take a written prompt and produce a moving image sequence, and the craft question of whether that sequence holds together as a film would.

children.name: Virtual Camera and Lensing
children.blurb: Virtual camera and lensing covers the simulated camera inside a rendered or generated scene: its position, its movement, its focal length, its aperture, and the way light is bent through glass that may not exist.

children.name: Face Replacement and Digital Doubles
children.blurb: Face replacement and digital doubles cover the work of putting one performer's face onto another body, or building a synthetic performer that stands in for a real one across a shot, a scene or an entire production.

children.name: Storyboarding and Pre-visualization
children.blurb: Storyboarding and pre-visualization cover the planning stage of a moving image project, where shots, camera moves, timing and staging are worked out before principal photography or full rendering begins.

children.name: Frame Interpolation and Restoration
children.blurb: Frame interpolation and restoration covers the work of repairing and smoothing moving images: removing dirt, scratches, noise and compression artefacts from old or damaged footage, and generating new frames between existing ones so that material shot at a low frame rate plays back smoothly.

sections.body: This section covers systems that generate moving images from text prompts, stills, or existing footage, and the tools that shape those images as if a camera and crew had been involved. In practice, text to video models turn a written description into a short clip, often a few seconds, with the model inventing motion, lighting, and camera movement on its own. Virtual lensing lets a creator specify focal length, depth of field, and camera moves without a physical camera, and digital doubles place a generated or scanned face onto a performer or a fully synthetic body. Storyboarding tools generate shot lists and pre-visual sequences before anything is shot, and frame interpolation fills the gaps between existing frames to smooth motion or raise frame rate. The site tracks 1000 video models alongside 1000 image models, which reflects how much of this work now sits on top of still image generation.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Short clips of a few seconds are now routine and often convincing, especially for landscapes, product shots, and simple action. Longer sequences remain unreliable because models lose track of objects, physics, and identity across shots, so continuity is still largely a human editing job. Digital doubles work well for brief appearances and background performers, and poorly for sustained close-ups where skin, eyes, and micro-expression give the synthesis away. Frame interpolation is mature for moderate motion and produces visible warping or ghosting around fast movement, occlusion, and fine detail like hair or hands. Restoration has improved markedly for scratches, noise, and low resolution, though it can also invent detail that was never in the source, which matters for archival and evidentiary use. Legal exposure is real and unsettled, with 92 active intellectual property lawsuits tracked on this site, and the training data and likeness rights behind these tools are still being tested in court.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Text to Video, Physics and Continuity for the core generation problem and why long shots fall apart, since almost everything else here depends on that base. Virtual Camera and Lensing is the page for anyone treating the model as a camera, covering focal length, depth of field, and movement as controllable parameters rather than accidents of the prompt. Face Replacement and Digital Doubles goes deeper into performer identity, likeness, and the consent and rights questions that follow, which connects directly to the litigation the site tracks. Storyboarding and Pre-visualization is the planning page, aimed at directors and artists who want generated shots before committing to production. Frame Interpolation and Restoration is the cleanup and repair page, for raising frame rates, smoothing motion, and recovering older or damaged footage. Read together, they follow the pipeline from idea to shot to finished frame.
